title: Bound for large low degree Fourier coefficients
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\{−1,1\}^n$. For each subset $S$ of the coordinates, let $\widehat g(S)$ be the uniform Fourier coefficient of the degree-at-most-$k$ part $g$ of $f$, and let $\|g\|_1=\sum_S|\widehat g(S)|$. Given real numbers $\varepsilon,L$ with $\varepsilon>0$ and $L\ge0$, if $\|g\|_1\le L$, then the number of subsets $S$ satisfying $\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\le \|g\|_1|\widehat g(S)|$ is at most $4L^2/\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube $\{−1,1\}^n$
the Fourier one-norm of the degree-at-most-$k$ part of $f$ is at most $L$
